articles.title: Global Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) Framework and India's Governance Model
articles.summary: India advances open-source digital public infrastructure frameworks to enhance global financial inclusion and e-governance across developing nations.
prelims: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) incorporates digital identity, fast payment systems, and consent-based data sharing.
The G20 Framework for Digital Public Infrastructure Systems was formally recognized during India's G20 Presidency.
Open APIs serve as the core technological architecture behind India's Aadhaar, UPI, and Account Aggregator systems.
articles.mains: Use as a key case study in GS-2 Governance and International Relations to illustrate India's soft power diplomacy and technology-driven public service delivery models.

articles.title: Operationalization of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)
articles.summary: Bureau of Energy Efficiency releases targeted guidelines for carbon intensity reductions across energy-intensive industrial sectors.
prelims: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) acts as the primary administrator and regulatory body for CCTS in India.
CCTS encompasses both compliance mechanism targets for specific sectors and a voluntary carbon trading market.
The Green Credit Program operates independently from CCTS to incentivize broader ecological actions beyond carbon mitigation.
articles.mains: Incorporate in GS-3 Economy and Environment questions regarding market-based mechanisms for industrial decarbonization and achievement of India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).

articles.title: Deep Sea Mining Regulations and India's Samudrayaan Mission Progress
articles.summary: International Seabed Authority reviews environmental safeguards as India prepares deep-submergence vehicle MATSYA 6000 for ocean mineral exploration.
prelims: MATSYA 6000 is an indigenous crewed deep-submergence vehicle developed by the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT).
India holds exclusive rights granted by the International Seabed Authority (ISA) for exploring polymetallic nodules in the Central Indian Ocean Basin.
Polymetallic nodules contain critical minerals such as nickel, cobalt, copper, and manganese essential for energy transition.
articles.mains: Analyze in GS-3 Science & Tech and Environment papers on the balance between resource extraction for clean energy technology and marine biodiversity preservation.

articles.title: Central Asian Flyway Action Plan under the Bonn Convention
articles.summary: India leads regional coordination initiatives under the Convention on Migratory Species to safeguard wetland habitats along the Central Asian Flyway.
prelims: The Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS) is commonly known as the Bonn Convention.
CMS functions under the aegis of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
The Central Asian Flyway (CAF) spans 30 countries and covers crucial wintering grounds for migratory birds across India.
articles.mains: Use in GS-3 Environment and Biodiversity answers regarding transboundary conservation strategies and international environmental treaties.

articles.title: Electoral Reform Recommendations on Decriminalization under RPA, 1951
articles.summary: Discussions highlight legal amendments needed under the Representation of the People Act to address pending criminal charges among political candidates.
prelims: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 specifies disqualification criteria for legislators upon conviction.
In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court struck down Section 8(4) which protected convicted sitting legislators from immediate disqualification.
Article 324 of the Constitution vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.
articles.mains: Cite in GS-2 Polity answers concerning electoral integrity, institutional reforms, and legal mechanisms to curb the criminalization of politics.
